kubernetes.reason: Part of the DataFlow extra: the disk class its stages' working volumes use.
The disk class of the directory's data volume, as a Kubernetes StorageClass name. AWS's term is the volume type.
Where an execution's Task credentials are read from, as a namespace. AWS runs a Task as the state machine's role, which the execution already names.
A node address the file share is served from. AWS's file systems are reached through mount targets in a subnet.
The disk class of the share, as a Kubernetes StorageClass name. AWS's term is the performance mode or storage class of the file system.
The namespace whose traffic is logged. AWS logs a VPC, subnet or network interface.
Which nodes capture the flow log. AWS captures it in the network fabric, with nothing to place.
The disk class of the migration's working volume, as a Kubernetes StorageClass name. AWS's term is the replication instance's storage.
Which nodes may host the gateway. AWS places a NAT gateway in the subnet it names.
The disk class of the stream's storage, as a Kubernetes StorageClass name. Kinesis exposes none.
The namespaces attached to the subnet. On AWS a resource names its subnet, not the other way round.
A Kubernetes Secret holding the user's console password. AWS sets it with CreateLoginProfile, which the console and the IAM API already serve.
The disk class of the pool's store, as a Kubernetes StorageClass name. Cognito exposes none.
The disk class an image is stored on, as a Kubernetes StorageClass name. EC2's term is the snapshot's storage tier.
The namespaces attached to the VPC. On AWS a resource names its VPC, not the other way round.

Account.reason: An account of the install's organization. Its object is cluster-wide and the operator's.

DataClassification.reason: A data classification level a resource carries (who may read it, how long it is kept). AWS has no resource for it: Macie reports findings, it does not hold a level.

DataFlow.reason: A graph of cross-engine data movements (sources, transforms, sinks) as one resource. AWS splits it across DMS tasks, Glue jobs and Kinesis streams, with no single resource for the graph.

* /api/iam/grants.how: iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:AttachGroupPolicy or iam:AttachRolePolicy, on the entity the grant names.

* /api/iam/users/{name}/password.how: iam:ChangePassword on the caller's own user, iam:UpdateLoginProfile on anyone else's (as AWS).

* /api/k8s.how: The console's resource API. Each request is the AWS action the kinds table maps it to (a resource type's own action on its ARN); every other object is the operator's (openinfra-operator:*, the management account's AdministratorAccess alone); anything unmapped is refused.

* /api/sts/switch-role.how: sts:AssumeRole on the role, decided by its trust policy (the console's Switch Role).

* /api/watch.how: The watched resource type's List action, as the kinds table maps it; the operator's objects are openinfra-operator:List*.
